passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Morning everyone. We have a long list today, so let's keep it moving. Release status first, then payments, support, the accessibility audit, the office move and the intern.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: After that a few newer things: the partner API limits, data retention, the survey, an invitation for Ben, and the on-call rota. Then the next sprint.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Aiko, how is the two point four release looking?

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Mostly good. All features are merged, but we still have the crash on older phones when you open the calendar view twice in a row.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: I can reproduce it every time on the test phone with the old operating system. It happens in about one out of three tries on the newer ones too.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Is that the date picker again or something new?

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: It's new. The calendar view keeps a reference to the old screen and the second open tries to reuse it after it's gone.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: How long would a fix take?

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Two days for the fix, maybe one more to be safe with the tests.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: And I need a full day to run the regression suite on the old phones after that.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Then we don't ship on Thursday. We hold the release until the crash is fixed and retested.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Fine by me. Nothing on the backend depends on that date.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Support would rather wait too. A crash in the calendar is the worst thing we could send to customers right now.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Okay, decided. Two point four waits for the crash fix.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: I'll fix the calendar crash by Wednesday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: And I'll rerun the regression suite on Thursday as soon as the build is there.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Good. Let's aim for the following Monday then, but only if Ben's run is clean.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Next, payments. Felix, you looked at the migration.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Yes. The current provider ends support for the old checkout in September. We have to move to their new interface or switch providers.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Switching providers would mean new contracts, new fees and a security review. Moving to their new interface is mostly our work.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: What's your recommendation?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Stay with them and migrate in two phases. First the card payments in June, then the saved payment methods in August.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: From the mobile side, phase one is small. Phase two needs the new screens for saved cards.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Please don't touch saved cards during the summer peak. July is our busiest month.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: That's why I put it in August, after the peak.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Okay, we stay with the current provider and migrate in two phases, cards in June and saved methods in August.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Felix, can you write the migration plan with the dates?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Sure, I'll have the plan ready by next Friday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Put me down for the mobile part of phase two, I'll estimate the screens once I see the plan.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Thanks. Support backlog. Dalia?

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: We have about three hundred and forty open tickets. Two weeks ago it was two hundred.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Most of them are people who can't find how to move a booking. It's the same question again and again.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Could we put a move button directly on the booking screen? Right now it's hidden in the menu.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: That's a small change. I could do it in the next sprint.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: That would help a lot, but it won't clear the backlog we already have.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: What do you need to clear it?

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: One more person for six weeks. A temporary contract would be enough.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Okay. We hire a temp for support for six weeks. I'll talk to finance about the budget this afternoon.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Thank you. I can write the job ad today if that helps.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Yes please, write it today and I'll post it once finance says yes.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: And I'll take the move button into the next sprint.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Good. Accessibility audit.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: The external auditor offered two slots, the second week of May or the first week of June.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: May is too early. We still have the old colour scheme on half the screens.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Then June. Ben, can you book the first week of June with them?

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, I'll book it today.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Do we know what the audit costs? I don't remember it being in the budget.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: I don't know. It was discussed last year, but I'm not sure it was approved.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: We should find out before we sign anything.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Agreed. That's open for now; I'll check the budget and come back to it next week.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Office move. As you know, we move to the third floor at the end of the month.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: The device lab needs special care. There are forty test phones and the charging racks.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: I can help pack the phones, but someone should label every cable or we'll lose a day.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: I'll label the cables and pack the lab on the last Thursday of the month.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: The servers aren't affected, they stay in the data centre.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Will the support phones keep the same numbers?

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, the numbers stay the same. Facilities confirmed that.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Last item, the intern. We interviewed three people. Who did you like?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: The second candidate, the one who built the train timetable app. Clear thinking and good questions.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Same for me. The first one was strong too, but wanted to work on design, not code.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: I liked the second one as well. She asked about our testing, which almost nobody does.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Then we offer the internship to the second candidate.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: I'll send her the offer on Monday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Can she start in July? I'd like her in the payments work.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: I'll ask her when I send the offer.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Now the newer things. First, the partner API. Felix, you said two partners keep hitting the limit?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Yes. The travel agency partner and the ticket reseller both hit the hundred requests per minute limit every evening between six and eight.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: When they hit it, their customers see an error and the bookings fail. Last week that was about two hundred failed bookings.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: We get those tickets too. People think it's our app that is broken, not the partner's site.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Can't they just retry later? Most clients retry after a few seconds.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: The reseller does retry, but the travel agency shows the error straight away. We asked them to fix it, but that will take them months.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: What would you raise the limit to?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Three hundred per minute for those two keys. The servers can take it; we're at forty percent at the evening peak.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: My worry is that we don't see per-key traffic today. If one partner goes wild, we only notice when everything is slow.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: That's fair. I can add per-key monitoring with an alert at eighty percent of the limit. It's about two days of work.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Then let's do it in that order. We raise the limit to three hundred for those two partners, but only once the per-key monitoring is live.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Okay. I'll have the monitoring and the alert in place by the fifteenth.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Should we charge for the higher limit? Other companies sell it as a premium tier.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Maybe, but that's a question for the partnership team, not for us today. Let's leave it open.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: I'll mention it to them, but I don't promise anything.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Next, data retention. Legal sent a request on Monday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: They want us to stop keeping booking logs forever. Their proposal is eighteen months, then delete.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Today the logs go back six years. That's about four terabytes in the archive.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Does the app use old logs for anything? I think the booking history screen reads from the database, not from the logs.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Right, the history screen doesn't touch the logs. Only the fraud checks look back, and they use ninety days at most.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Then eighteen months is plenty. I'd only ask that we keep the test fixtures that were built from logs, but those are anonymised already.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Okay. We adopt the eighteen months that legal proposed.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: I'd delete in two steps: first everything older than three years, then the rest down to eighteen months a month later. If something breaks, we see it early.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Good idea. Two steps, starting with the logs older than three years.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: I'll write the deletion job and run the first step at the start of next month.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: And I'll update the privacy page in the help centre so it says eighteen months.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: What about the backups? If the logs are in last year's backups, are they really deleted?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Good question. I don't know what legal expects there.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Let's ask legal. Dalia, you have the thread with them, can you ask whether the backups count?

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, I'll ask them this week.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: The customer survey results came in on Friday. Dalia, the short version?

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Three hundred and twelve answers. Overall satisfaction went down a little, from eight point one to seven point six.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: The biggest complaint, by far, is notifications. People get three reminders for every booking and many find that too much.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Three is the default because of the no-shows. The product team said fewer reminders means more people forget.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Do we have numbers on that? I remember the test last year showed almost no difference between one and three reminders.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: I think it was about one percent more no-shows with a single reminder. I'd have to check the report.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: One percent against our biggest complaint. I think the answer is clear. We go down to one reminder by default, and people who want more can turn them on.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: No objection from the backend. It's a setting, the scheduler already supports it.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: The settings screen needs a small change, but it's easy. I'll do it in the next sprint, after the move button.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: I'll write to the customers who complained the loudest, there were five of them, and tell them it's coming.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Thanks. Anything else from the survey?

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: A few people asked for a dark mode. Not many, maybe fifteen.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Dark mode is a big job with the old colour scheme still around. After the accessibility work it would be much easier.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Then not now. Let's look at dark mode again after the audit.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: I could maybe look at how other apps word their reminder settings, if I find time this week.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Ben, you mentioned an invitation to speak?

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, a testing meetup in October asked me to give a talk about how we test on old phones.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: It's a small conference, about two hundred people, but a good place to find testers. They pay the hotel, not the flight.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: We've been trying to hire a second tester for months. That sounds worth it.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: I agree. Go, and we pay the flight.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Great. I'll send them the abstract by the end of next week.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: If you want, I can review the slides before you go.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, please, that would help.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Last of the new items: on-call. We had three pages at night last week and all of them went to Felix.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: It's fine once in a while, but not every week. And two of the three were the disk alarm on staging, which shouldn't page anyone.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: Staging shouldn't page at night at all. Can we move those alerts to email?

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, I'll move the staging alerts to email tonight, together with the disk cleanup.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: And for the real pages, we rotate. One week each, Felix and Aiko first, then Ben joins after the release.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Okay for me, as long as we get a day off after a night with a page.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: That's fair. A day off after any night page. I'll write the rota and send it by Friday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: Does support need to be in the rota?

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: No, support stays nine to six. The rota is only for the systems.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Okay, the next sprint. My proposal: the calendar crash, the move button, and phase one of payments.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: That's a lot for one sprint, but the crash is two days and the button is one, so it fits.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: Phase one of payments won't be finished in one sprint. I can start it.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Fine, phase one starts this sprint and continues in the next one.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: From support, the move button is the most important thing on that list.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: From testing, I need the crash fix first so I can plan the regression run.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Agreed. Crash first, then the button, then payments.

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: And the reminder setting right after the button, if there's room.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Yes, if there's room.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: One more thing. The staging server is running out of disk space. It's at ninety two percent.

passages.speaker: Speaker 2 (remote)
passages.text: I'll clean up the old builds tonight.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Thanks, Felix. Anything else from anyone?

passages.speaker: Speaker 3 (remote)
passages.text: Just that the design team asked for feedback on the new icons by Friday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 4 (remote)
passages.text: I sent mine yesterday.

passages.speaker: Speaker 5 (remote)
passages.text: I'll send mine tomorrow.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Okay. Let me sum up. We hold two point four for the crash fix. We stay with the payment provider and migrate in two phases.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: We hire a temp for support for six weeks. The audit is the first week of June, and its budget is still open.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: We move at the end of the month, and we offer the internship to the second candidate.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: On the newer items: the two partners get three hundred requests per minute once the monitoring is live, booking logs are kept for eighteen months, and reminders go down to one by default.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Ben gives the talk in October, on-call rotates weekly, and two things are still open: charging partners for the higher limit, and whether the backups count for the deletion.

passages.speaker: Speaker 1 (remote)
passages.text: Thanks everyone, see you next week.
